findings.description: CLOSED. ADR-022 clause 1 now defines a bounded enqueue-outcome vocabulary on IWorkHintSink's result-returning call: Accepted / Coalesced / InFlight / Overflow / Stopped, with the boolean TryEnqueue retained for the callers that only need enqueued-or-not. Clause 2 defines the exact cursor-advance rule: Accepted, Coalesced and InFlight are all covered and continue; Overflow and Stopped stop the run at that item; a correctly-no-work item is covered and does not stall; the run persists the position after the last covered item and wraps at the end. This establishes a contiguous covered prefix and a provable successive-run coverage guarantee, and the rejected-alternatives section explicitly rejects boolean-count advance.

CLOSED. ADR-022 clause 3 replaces the integer offset with a stable opaque (SortName, itemId) seek key over a total order with an item-id tie-break, and IMediaLibraryEnumerator gains a resume capability that returns the page strictly after the key (a host query predicate where supported, otherwise a bounded linear skip). Add/remove does not reset the cursor; only a scope change does. The guarantee is honestly bounded: guaranteed for a stable library and best-effort under concurrent mutation, with no stable item skipped across a full cycle. Plan F4 acceptance and tasks 19.1/19.2 require the stable-seek-key and library-mutation cases.

CLOSED. ADR-023 clause 3 requires the re-enqueue to happen after the in-flight slot is released: record the stale-basis discard, call CompleteProcessing(item.Key), then enqueue the fresh current-version item, dropping when stopped/full. It requires a coverage test that fails if the re-enqueue is issued before the slot is released. Plan F6 acceptance and task 19.4 repeat the pre-slot-release failing test.

CLOSED. ADR-023 clause 1 defines a bounded DiscardReason (ConfigurationStale, ItemMissing, Ineligible, ConnectionChanged, IdentityUnavailable); ConfigurationStale covers both the initial version check and the pre-publication version re-check. Clause 2 states that exactly one classification, ConfigurationStale, re-enqueues, bounded to one per (item, connection, surface, version); every other classification, a same-version discard, and a stopped/full queue do not. Plan F6 and tasks 19.3/19.4 require a test that a non-version discard does not re-enqueue, and the rejected alternatives explicitly reject a worker-side version comparison.

CLOSED. ADR-024 clause 1 narrows NoDisplayableValue to mean exactly the resolved BadgeSelection being empty, and adds a distinct bounded pass-through reason NoFittingBadge for a non-empty selection whose layout is empty after shorten/omit. Clause 5 preserves the other reasons including NoFittingBadge. Plan F7 acceptance and tasks 20.1/20.2 require a coverage test that a non-empty selection which cannot fit performs no mutation. This removes the ambiguity that made a layout failure remove a correct badge.

findings.area: ADR-028 (G6/DG-15): MB/KB unit-selection rule and min round-trip
findings.description: CLOSED. ADR-028 clause 1 fixes the unit per field in code (binary MB for every byte limit, binary KB for WebhookMaxPayloadBytes), a per-field step S that divides minimum/default/maximum (64 KiB for the three 64-KiB-min fields; 1 MiB or 1 KiB otherwise), a per-field display precision P (4 fractional digits for the 64-KiB-step MB fields; 0 otherwise), an explicit range label that stays in the field's unit across the 1 MiB boundary, and a scaled-decimal conversion algorithm. Every minimum/default/maximum is an exact multiple of its step, so all values round-trip exactly, including 64 KiB -> 0.0625 MB -> 65536 bytes. Verified against the actual validation ranges and defaults.

findings.area: ADR-023 (F6/DG-20): bound storage and clause-2 eligibility claim
findings.description: CLOSED. ADR-023 clause 4 defines the bound as implicit in the version carried by the re-enqueued item (the fresh item carries the current version, so ConfigurationStale can never recur and a same-version repeat is impossible; no separate version set is needed; effective bound one per (item, connection, surface, version)). Clause 5 restates the eligibility ordering accurately: the version check precedes item resolve/eligibility, so an ineligible/absent item is re-enqueued once and then discarded for its real reason with no further re-enqueue.

findings.area: ADR-024 (F7/DG-21): restore entry point and location

No second path is introduced and the per-subject gate/recovery suite is not bypassed. Clause 3 confirms a Normal-fence restoration is intended and crash-recoverable via ArtworkRecoveryDecisions/ArtworkReconciler. Plan F7 decision and task 20.1 repeat the entry point and fence.

findings.description: NOTED. ADR-028 clause 1 states that 'a value that does not land on the step is rejected by the existing bounded validation rather than silently rounded.' The existing bounded validation (OperationalLimits.Validate) checks range only, and the current config.html byte inputs use integer pattern + byte min/max with no step. A fraction such as 0.1 MB for a 64-KiB-step field would compute 104858 bytes, which is in range but not step-aligned. The decision's intent (non-step values rejected) is clear and does not affect the min/default/max round-trip, so this is not a reopening of AR-V12-06; task 16.1 should implement an explicit step check (or a browser step constraint enforced on submit) and the ADR wording should not attribute it to the existing range validation.
findings.recommended_action: Reword clause 1 to require an explicit per-field step check in the settings conversion/validation path (and, where the page uses native constraint validation, the step attribute), rather than attributing step rejection to the existing bounded range validation; task 16.1 already owns the conversion helper.

recommendation: CHANGES_REQUIRED, narrowly scoped. The reworked ADR-022..ADR-028 genuinely close all 25 attempt-1 findings: AR-V12-01/02 now establish and honestly bound the F4 coverage guarantee (bounded enqueue-outcome vocabulary, contiguous covered-prefix advance rule, stable (SortName, itemId) seek key with a resume-capable enumerator); AR-V12-03/04 make the F6 fix implementable and bounded (re-enqueue only after CompleteProcessing, a bounded DiscardReason with only ConfigurationStale re-enqueuing, and a test that fails if issued before release); AR-V12-05 discriminates on the empty resolved selection with a distinct NoFittingBadge so a layout failure never removes a correct badge; AR-V12-06 defines a per-field unit/step/precision mapping whose minima/defaults/maxima all round-trip exactly (including the 64 KiB minima). The MEDIUM items 07-15 are all addressed (Cache-authority cursor, post-save exclusion consistency, implicit version bound, ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync under the Normal fence, corrected ADR-026 clause-4 framing and full site list, mixed-capture classification with task 16.2 ownership, illustrative example set, and the Phase 17/18 documentation-checklist additions). The F5 Open->Accepted reclassification is consistent across open.md, accepted.md, 00-index.md, and state.json, and F5 is excluded from every v1.2 task. One open LOW finding remains: docs/implementation/planning/v1.2.json task 21.2's acceptance criterion still says 'F5 remains open', contradicting the accepted register and the user decision; it must be corrected. One INFORMATIONAL note (AR-V12-27) asks task 16.1 to own an explicit step-multiple check rather than attributing it to the existing range validation. With the task-21.2 line corrected (and the step check owned), the ADRs are sound to accept as-is; DG-19, DG-20, and DG-21 remain genuine user acceptance gates that must be accepted before the Phase 19/20 implementation tasks (19.1-19.4, 20.1-20.2) are selected.
summary: Independent re-review (attempt 2) of the reworked v1.2 planning package. All 25 attempt-1 findings are genuinely closed: the six HIGH findings (F4 coverage vocabulary/cursor rule and stable seek key; F6 post-release re-enqueue and bounded DiscardReason; F7 empty-selection discriminator; G6 unit/step/precision round-trip) and the nine MEDIUM findings (cursor Cache authority/kind/scope; post-save trigger consistency; ADR-023 implicit bound and eligibility ordering; ADR-024 restore entry point under the Normal fence; ADR-026 clause-4 framing and site enumeration; ADR-028 mixed-capture classification, illustrative example set, and task 16.2 ownership; Phase 17/18 doc-checklist additions) are correctly reflected in the ADRs, the plan, PLANS.md, and the planning record. The LOW/INFORMATIONAL items are applied, and AR-V12-23 is correctly not_required. The execution-order invariant holds (every task exactly once per phase; consistent across state.json, PLANS.md, and the planning record), every decision gate and deliverable has an owner, no historical ADR text or immutable history was rewritten, F5 is Accepted across the register/index/state and excluded from every v1.2 task, and scripts/check-docs.sh passes (with the generated-block check skipped because dotnet is unavailable, verified by hand). One new LOW open finding remains: the planning record's task 21.2 acceptance still says 'F5 remains open', contradicting the Accepted reclassification; one INFORMATIONAL note asks task 16.1 to own an explicit step-multiple check. Status: CHANGES_REQUIRED for that single-line correction; the ADRs themselves are sound to accept as-is, and DG-19/DG-20/DG-21 remain genuine user acceptance gates before the dependent Phase 19/20 implementation tasks.
